pr.title: feat(desktop): Review v2 stage 1 — GitHub slice and Keryx links
pr.body:
Desktop Review v2, stage 1 "GitHub slice and links" (Flow 517): the Pull requests and Issues boards group by GitHub data only, every card gets a Keryx work row, and sessions can be bound to a PR or Issue. Two review rounds are done and their findings fixed; owner choices and known gaps are listed below. Requirements: `docs/requirements/keryx-desktop-review-v2/` (PRD R1–R3, R5, R6, parts of R4 and R7; decisions D5, D6). Stage 0 was #1294. Current state and deviations: section "Состояние этапа 1" of `implementation-plan.md`.

## What changes

- **Pull requests board, GitHub only (R1, R2, D6).** Groupings "Status" (default: Draft · Waiting for review · Changes requested · Approved; Merged and Closed only when the state filter includes them) and "My role" (Requested from me · Mine · Others). Quick filters "Requested from me", "Mine", "CI failed" sit in the context row, so the stage 0 toolbar measurements still hold. The attention and "In review" lanes are gone; the reason line uses GitHub data only.
- **Keryx work row (R4 part, R7 part).** A fixed 24px row on every PR card and list row with Review (`Review · <state>` from `localReview`, no round or behind count), Flow (by `prUrl` or a bound session's `flow` flag) and Session slots (count, newest, menu with all and "New session"). An empty slot shows its labelled action. "Fix review comments" is stage 4.
- **Sessions bound to a Subject (R5).** `subject` `{kind, repo, number, url, repositoryId?}` in the session's `flags.json`, written through `_keryx/session_flags` under a per-session `flags.json.lock`. "Open in session" reopens the newest bound session or creates and binds one, prefilling the PR URL without sending. The session header links to the PR or Issue and its Flow. Issue sessions get `subject` from `withIssueBinding`; sessions an older keryx bound without one are backfilled on the next open unless the person unlinked it.
- **Older keryx.** keryx stores a new session only after its first turn, so the notice "binding was not saved" appears after that turn at the latest; the session keeps working.
- **Work from a bound session (R6).** `/review` with no target preselects the bound PR. "Create Flow" opens the bound session with a prefilled flow prompt. When exactly one new flow package appears within 15 minutes while exactly one request with a filled prompt is pending, the PR work row asks "Link Flow #N?" with Link and Dismiss. Only Link writes the session's `flow` flag; Dismiss, several new packages or several pending requests link nothing (AC9 as re-frozen in round 2).
- **Issues (R3, D5).** Default source "Project repository" (`keryx issues list` with `source: "repository"`, `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`, pull requests dropped, up to 3 pages per load); a stored choice wins. Lanes Open · Closed by GitHub state. The Flow stage filter is gone; the work row has Flow and Session slots ("Open in session"). If the default source is unavailable (no GitHub.com remote, Issues turned off → 410, or an older keryx), the board shows the reason and "Show issues assigned to me", plus an update hint for an older keryx.

No Rust changes. User docs: `docs/docs/guides/desktop-issues.md`, `docs/docs/cli-reference.md` (`issues`).

## Verification

At head (after fix round 2):

- `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `bun test src`: 1051 pass, 0 fail.
- Root `bunx tsc --noEmit -p .`: clean. Root focused suites: 44 pass, 0 fail.
- The scenario "PR without Flow and review → Open in session → `/review` → review link on the card" is an App-level test; named mutants from both review rounds are red.
- Stage 0 attention set: no lines edited in either fix round.

Not verified: no run in the real app with real GitHub data; work row in narrow lanes, session menu placement, list width (1000px) and the LY-002/LY-004 widths not measured; lint and the Rust CI path not run locally.

## Review

- Round 1 (head 6a2a3031f): 32 findings (2 blocker, 6 major); fixed in a34d8961b.
- Round 2 (head 88e3faba9): 44 findings (1 blocker, 3 major); HL-001 decided by the owner (confirmed link instead of a silent one); fixed in 80ef58bd5 and c4e8e3e24.
- Packages: `.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-github-com-mrciphersmith-keryx-pull-1300` and `…-pull-1300-r02`. Decisions: the Flow 517 journal.

## Choices for the owner

Taken by the orchestrator during the fix rounds; each can be reverted:

- Create Flow waits 15 minutes from the press, not "until the next turn".
- A shown "Link Flow #N?" does not expire; Dismiss also stops offering that package.
- A session switch while "Open in session" runs leaves no prompt and no pending request; a repeat press during an open reuses it without a prompt.
- New PR sessions also count a Flow found through a bound session; the launch dialog preselects the newest of several Flows.
- Review progress shows only in the slot title; the "Transcript updated" stamp left the card.
- A header link to a PR of another repository shows a banner and stays armed until that repository is shown.
- Warn tone for "needs answer" and "publication pending"; a merged PR keeps the "publication pending" text without the warn tone.
- "Show issues assigned to me" appears only for the default (not yet chosen) source.
- Issues load up to 3 GitHub pages when a page holds only pull requests.
- A flags write waits up to 3 s for the lock, then fails with "retry".
- Subject backfill can re-link once a session unlinked before this version (no unlink marker then).
- Earlier UI choices: review slot state words; disabled "Run review" on merged or closed PRs; session menu button "More"; "not saved yet" for an unsaved session; "Create Flow" replaces the composer draft; Issue card buttons became work-row links.

## Known gaps

- Deviation (a), team review requests for the tab indicator, stays open; (b) is unchanged until stage 2.
- An Issue has no "another or new session" choice: the binding backend keeps one session per issue and account.
- A Flow created outside the Create Flow window, or with two or more requests pending, is not offered; it shows on the PR once it has a `prUrl`.
- `subject` names no GitHub account, so issue sessions bound under different accounts count together. GitHub Enterprise issues get no `subject`.
- Deferred info findings: PF-006/HW2-002, AR-002, AR-004..006, PF-002, LG-004, LY-002/LY-004, UX-003..006 (round 2 package).

Flow package: `.metaproject/flows/517-2026-11-23-desktop-review-v2-stage-1-github-slice-a/`. Still to do: the merge decision.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: The PR lane function reads no field of the local review: a model test iterates every local review state (none, queued, running, awaiting answer, ready, partial, publication pending, outdated) for the same GitHub card and gets the same lane; the attention lane and the Keryx "In review" lane no longer exist (R1, D6, spec AC1) · sensitive: mutation [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review/model.test.ts`]

AC2: On the Pull requests board, a local review starting, finishing or being published changes neither the lane, the position nor the visibility of the card (a DOM test updates `localReview` on a shown card and asserts the same lane and index); cards are ordered by `updatedAt` descending (R1) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review/ReviewBoard.dom.test.tsx`]

AC3: Default grouping "Status" shows Draft · Waiting for review (no decision or REVIEW_REQUIRED) · Changes requested · Approved, with Merged and Closed only when the state filter includes them; grouping "My role" shows Requested from me · Mine · Others; quick filters "Requested from me", "Mine" and "CI failed" narrow the board; every shown card satisfies all filters and the search (no active-review bypass, a test with an active review and a non-matching author shows nothing); a lane that cannot hold a card under the current filters is not drawn (R2, spec AC2, AC13) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review`]
AC4: The card reason line is derived from GitHub data only; Keryx review state appears only in the work row [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review`]

AC5: Every PR card and list row renders a Keryx work row with exactly three slots (review, Flow, session) whose DOM structure is the same with zero and with three links, and the row has a fixed height in `apps/desktop/src/styles/review.css`; the review slot shows the state from `localReview` without a round number or behind count and opens the current review panel; the Flow slot shows "Flow #<id> · <stage>" and opens the Flow; empty slots show the labelled actions "Run review", "Create Flow", "Open in session" (R4 part, R7, spec AC14) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review`]

AC6: Every action on a PR card, PR list row and Issue card has a visible text label (a DOM test asserts non-empty text content for each action control); "Fix review comments" is not shown in this stage (R7 part, spec AC15 part) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review src/issues`]

AC7: "Open in session" on a PR with no bound session creates a new session bound to the PR Subject and prefills the composer with the PR URL without sending it; pressing it again opens the same session (newest non-archived bound session); the session slot menu lists the bound sessions and "New session", which creates another bound session (R5, spec AC8 part) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src`]

AC8: Subject storage: `_keryx/session_flags` accepts `subject` {kind "pr"|"issue", repo, number, url, optional repositoryId}, refuses an invalid one, persists it in `flags.json` so a fresh read (restart) returns it, and `null` unlinks it; an Issue session bound by `withIssueBinding` carries `subject.kind = "issue"`; when keryx stores the session but replies without `subject` (older keryx), Desktop keeps the session open and shows a notice that the binding was not saved, at the latest after the session's first turn (spec AC8, failure scenario) [verify: exec `bun test src/session/organize.test.ts src/acp/shell-session-organize.test.ts src/session/issues`]

AC9: "Create Flow" on a PR card opens the PR-bound session with a prefilled flow prompt naming the PR URL; when exactly one new flow package appears while exactly one Create Flow request with a filled prompt is pending (bounded window), the PR work row offers "Link Flow #<id>?" with Link and Dismiss; only Link writes the session `flow` flag, after which the Flow shows on that PR card; Dismiss, several new packages or several pending requests link nothing (R6) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src`]

AC10: In a PR-bound session, `/review` without a target opens the launch dialog with that PR preselected, and the review started there appears as the review link on that PR card without a manual refresh (R6, spec AC9) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src`]

AC11: Issues board default grouping is by GitHub state (Open · Closed, Closed drawn only when the state filter includes closed issues); GitHub Project grouping is unchanged; the Flow stage filter is gone; issues without a Flow are spread over the GitHub columns (R3, spec AC12) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/issues`]

AC12: Each Issue card has a work row with a Flow slot (link with stage, or "Create Flow") and a session slot (bound sessions found through `subject`, or "Open in session") [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/issues`]

AC13: The default Issues source is the project repository: `keryx issues list` with `source: "repository"` lists `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues` of the repository resolved from the project cwd and excludes pull requests; "Assigned to me" and the other sources stay selectable and a stored source preference wins (D5) [verify: exec `bun test src/integrations/issues-board.test.ts && cd apps/desktop && bun test src/issues`]

AC14: The Pull requests tab attention set and indicator are preserved: `ReviewBoard.dom.test.tsx` passes, and every edited line in `carriedAttention`, `seeded`, `seedFor`, `attentionPrs` or `stale` handling has a recorded one-line mutation that fails a test (journal) · sensitive: mutation [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review/ReviewBoard.dom.test.tsx`]

AC15: `attachBadges` (`src/review/desk-run-store.ts`) and `localBadge` (`src/review/board-badges.ts`) still agree [verify: exec `bun test src/review/desk-run-store.test.ts src/review/board-badges.test.ts`]

AC16: Scenario "PR without Flow and review → Open in session → `/review` → review link on the card" passes as one integrated test over the App wiring (bound session created, launch dialog preselects the PR, the started run shows on the card) [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src`]

AC17: The Pull requests toolbar keeps the stage 0 behaviour: no element added to `.flows-toolbar`, or, if one is added, the board toolbar is re-measured at the stage 0 widths and the result recorded in the journal [verify: judged]
AC18: Desktop typecheck and the full Desktop test suite pass [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit && bun test src`]
AC19: Deviation (a) (team review requests) stays open because stage 1 introduces no team membership; the implementation plan records it [verify: none — documentation statement, checked in review]

entries.title: gdctx-flag-allowlist-no-bundle-expansion
entries.summary: A per-flag string allowlist that doesn't expand POSIX-bundled short flags rejects the idiomatic form of a tool's own CLI habits (`-il` vs `-i -l`); expand-then-check, not check-then-reject, for any allowlisted boolean-flag set.

entries.title: Findings reach a review round through the report's keryx:findings block, and a round without one silently records none
entries.summary: `keryx review ingest --report <md>` reads structured findings from a fenced ` ```json keryx:findings ` block inside the report. A report without that block ingests as `findings: in=0`, and every `--verifications` claim naming one of its findings is then discarded as unresolvable — because the finding it names is not in the round.

entries.title: keryx-gdctx-gdgraph-routing-index-cost-not-measured-before-shipping
entries.summary: A mandatory context-injection rule's per-read cost multiplies by every subsequent turn and every subagent dispatch. Measure the re-billed cost across a realistic turn count and subagent fan-out before setting a rule's default scope, not just its one-time size.

entries.title: The keryx on PATH is a stale build; the review pipeline does not exercise the code under review
entries.summary: `~/.local/bin/keryx` is an installed build, and its version lags the working tree. It is NOT the working tree. Every `keryx …` invocation — including `keryx review ingest`, which is how a managed review package is recorded — runs that build, so the review pipeline routinely does not exercise the code being reviewed.

entries.title: A fix round needs its own review: three consecutive rounds each introduced a blocker
entries.summary: On PR #215 (flow 127, project registry) three consecutive review-fix rounds each introduced a new blocker while closing the previous one. The defect was not in any single fix; it was in treating a fix as finished once it addressed the reported symptom.

entries.title: Theme switch repaints already-rendered chrome via old-slot value matching
entries.summary: `/theme` in the OpenTUI shell applied and persisted correctly on 0.2.66, but `applyTheme` (src/tui/shell-chrome.ts) only recolored the chrome's OWN surfaces (renderer background, sidebar border, docks, composer, `/`-menu). Every renderable painted EARLIER with `getTheme()` — transcript frames (user echoes, code-segment boxes, block bodies, side-worker boxes), tone-colored block headers (`theme.error`/`theme.tool`), dock/queue-dock buttons, sidebar panels — kept the old palette's hex in its `borderColor`/`backgroundColor`/`fg` props, so a dark→dark switch (groknight↔tokyonight) looked like "the theme did not apply". Fix: on every `applyTheme`, walk the renderable trees (transcript, docks, sidebarTop, menu, composer, header, footer) and rewrite any prop whose color equals an OLD theme slot hex to the NEW slot hex.

entries.title: A shell allowlist matched against the raw command string is not a security boundary
entries.summary: A remembered glob pattern that is matched against a command string which is then handed to `/bin/sh -c` grants far more than it appears to. The pattern matches text; the shell re-interprets that text. Verified, not theorised: a live allowlist contained `bash *`, `python3 *`, `curl *`, `cd *`, `# *`, `docker *`, `sudo *`, and the exact string `rm -rf /` — each an arbitrary-execution grant that auto-approved with no prompt.

entries.title: SAC: Напиши мне скрипт на питоне цикла от 1 до 10 с промежутка…
entries.summary: Session fixed /theme perception bug: applyTheme in shell-chrome.ts now repaints already-rendered chrome (transcript frames, tone block headers, dock buttons, sidebar panels) via themeColorToHex/themeColorRemap/recolorThemeTree, because OpenTUI stores colors as RGBA objects. Committed a6dd8dd, pushed to main. Lesson already accepted directly: .metaproject/memory/lessons/theme-switch-repaint.md (created via keryx memory new, bypassing SAC because no slate was open). This proposal records the work for review/audit.
